711205.full: ῥαφίς, -ίδος, ἡ (ῥάπτω, to sew), a needle: Mat.19:24, Mrk.10:25 (cf. βελόνη).† (AS)

s: anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge
711209.full: 1. the lower part of the back, the chine , (Iliad by Homer): then, the spine or backbone , ὑπὸ ῥάχιν παγῆναι to be impaled, (Aeschulus Tragicus) 2. anything ridged like the backbone, a mountain-ridge , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

711241.full: ῥέω [in LXX chiefly for זוּב ;] to flow: Jhn.7:38 (cf. παραρρέω).† (AS)

711242.full: ῥῆγμα, -τος, τό (ῥήγνυμι), [in LXX: 3Ki.11:30-31 12:24, 4Ki.2:12 (קֶרַע), Amo.6:12 (11) A (בְּקִיעַ) * ;] __1. cl. (and so in LXX), a fracture; then by meton., that which is torn. __2. In NT, ruin: Luk.6:49.† (AS)

711243.lxx: in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע, also for קָרַע, etc.
711243.full: ῥήγνυμι and (Mrk.9:18) ῥήσσω, [in LXX chiefly for בָּקַע, also for קָרַע, etc. ;] __1. to rend, break asunder: Mat.7:6, Mrk.2:22, Luk.5:37; pass., Mat.9:17. __2. Of the voice, with accusative, φωνήν, etc. (Hdt., al.), to break forth into speech: absol., Gal.4:27 (LXX). __3. = ῥήσσω (Dem., al.), to throw or dash down: Mrk.9:18, Luk.9:42 (cf. δια-, περι-, προσ-ρήγνυμι).† SYN.: θραύω, κατάγνυμι (AS)

711246.lxx: in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, also for פֶּה, and Aram. פִּתְגָּם, etc.
711246.full: ῥῆμα, -τος, τό [in LXX chiefly for דָּבָר, also for פֶּה, and Aram. פִּתְגָּם, etc. ;] __1. prop., of that which is said or spoken, __(a) a word: Mat.27:14, 2Co.12:4; pl., τὰ ῥ., of speech, discourse, Luk.7:1, Jhn.8:20, Act.2:14, Rom.10:18, 2Pe.3:2, al.; __(b) opposite to ὄνομα (a single word), a saying, statement, word of prophecy, instruction or command (in cl., phrase): Mat.26:75, Mrk.9:32, Luk.1:38 2:50, Act.11:16, Rom.10:8, Heb.11:3; ῥ. θεοῦ (κυρίου), Luk.3:2, Act.11:16, Eph.6:17, Heb.6:5 11:3, 1Pe.1:25" (LXX) ; τὰ ῥ. τ. θεοῦ, Jhn.3:34 8:47; ῥ. ἀργόν, Mat.12:36;ῥ. ἄρρητα, 2Co.12:4. __2. Like Heb. דָּבָר (but perh. also a Gk. colloquialism, see Kennedy, Sources, 124; Thackeray, Gr., 41), of that which is the subject of speech, a thing, matter (Gen.15:1, Deu.17:8, al.): Luk.1:37 2:15, Act.10:37; pl., Luk.1:65 2:19, 51, Act.5:32 13:42 (AS)

711248.full: Resh, the 20th letter of the Hebrew alphabet; used in LXX for acrostic Psalms such as Psa.119

s: passage, a speech in a play
711250.full: 1. a saying, speaking, speech , (Odyssey by Homer), etc.; ἡ ἀπὸ Σκυθῶν ῥῆσις the Scythian phrase , (Herdotus Historicus) 2. a resolution, declaration , (Herdotus Historicus) 3. a tale, legend , (Pindar) 4. a phrase or passage, a speech in a play , (Aristophanes Comicus) (ML)

s: on stated terms, on certain conditions
711253.full: 1. stated, specified , (Iliad by Homer); ἐς χρόνον ῥητόν at a set or stated time, (Herdotus Historicus); ἡμέραι ῥ. (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς γέρασι with fixed prerogatives, (Thucydides); ῥ. ἀργύριον a stated sum, (Thucydides); ἐπὶ ῥητοῖς on stated terms, on certain conditions , (Herdotus Historicus):—;adverb ῥητῶς, expressly, distinctly , (New Testament) 2. spoken of, known, famous , (Hesiod) 3. that may be spoken or told , (Aeschulus Tragicus); ῥητὸν ἄρρητόν τ᾽ ἔπος, Lat. fas nefasque, (Sophocles Tragicus) 4. in Mathem., ῥητά are rational quantities , opposite to surds ἄλογα); (Plato Philosophus) (ML)

711260.full: ῥίζα, -ης, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for שָׁרַשׁ ;] a root: Mat.3:10, Luk.3:9; ἐκ ῥιζῶν, Mrk.11:20; ῥ. ἔχειν, Mat.13:6, Mrk.4:6; id. before ἐν ἑαυτῷ, figuratively, Mat.13:21, Mrk.4:17, Luk.8:13. Metaphorical (as in various senses in cl.), of cause, origin, source, etc.; __(a) of things, ῥ. πάντων τ. κακῶν (Eur.), 1Ti.6:10; __(b) of persons: of ancestors, Rom.11:16-18; ῥ. πικρίας, Heb.12:15. Of that which springs from a root, a shoot; metaphorically, of offspring, Rom.15:12 (LXX) Rev.5:5 22:16.† (AS)

711261.full: ῥιζόω, -ῶ (ῥίζα), [in LXX: Isa.40:24, Jer.12:2 (שָׁרַשׁ), Sir.3:28 24:12 * ;] to cause to take root. Metaphorical, to plant, fix firmly, establish: pass. (EV, rooted), ἐν ἀγάπῃ, Eph.3:18(17); ἐν Χριστῷ, Col.2:7 (cf. ἐκ ριζόω).† (AS)

s: to be tossed or blown by the wind
711264.full: ῥιπίζω (ῥιπίς, a fan) [in LXX: Dan LXX 2:35 (נְשָׂא) * ;] primarily, to fan a fire, hence generally, to make a breeze (Plut., al.). In pass. (cf. Philo, de inter. round., 24), to be tossed or blown by the wind: of waves, ἀνεμιζομένῳ καὶ ῥιπιζομένῳ, blown and raised with the wind (Hort, in l), Jas.1:6.† (AS)

711266.lxx: in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi.
711266.full: ῥιπτέω, see: ῥίπτω. ῥίπτω and (Act.22:23) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; see Veitch, see word ῥίπτω, fin.), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi. ;] __1. to throw, cast, hurl: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.27:5, Act.27:19, 29; with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:30, Luk.4:35; pass., Luk.17:2; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, cast down, prostrate (Polyb., al.): Mat.9:36; of garments, to throw off (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, 1Ma.5:43; so EV in Act.22:23, but see infr.). __2. = ῥιπτάζω, to shake, toss, throw about: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.22:23 (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l; Field, Notes, 136; but see supr.).† (AS)

711267.lxx: in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi.
711267.full: ῥίπτω and (Act.22:23) ῥιπτέω (strengthened form; see Veitch, see word ῥίπτω, fin.), [in LXX chiefly for שָׁלַךְ hi. ;] __1. to throw, cast, hurl: with accusative of thing(s), Mat.27:5, Act.27:19, 29; with accusative of person(s), Mat.15:30, Luk.4:35; pass., Luk.17:2; ptcp., ἐριμμένοι, cast down, prostrate (Polyb., al.): Mat.9:36; of garments, to throw off (for flight, Eur., Xen., al.; ὅπλα, 1Ma.5:43; so EV in Act.22:23, but see infr.). __2. = ῥιπτάζω, to shake, toss, throw about: τ. ἱμάτια, Act.22:23 (EGT, Page, Rackham, in l; Field, Notes, 136; but see supr.).† (AS)

s: a knob shaped like a pomegranate
711272.full: 1. ionic and epic ῥοιή, a pomegranate-tree , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the fruit, a pomegranate , (Homeric Hymns) 3. a knob shaped like a pomegranate , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

s: a knob shaped like a pomegranate
711273.full: 1. ionic and epic ῥοιή, a pomegranate-tree , (Odyssey by Homer) 2. the fruit, a pomegranate , (Homeric Hymns) 3. a knob shaped like a pomegranate , (Herdotus Historicus) (ML)

711282.full: the isle of Rhodes , (Iliad by Homer), etc. (ML)

711285.full: to whistle , Lat. stridere, (Iliad by Homer); of a snake, to hiss , (Hesiod):—;Pass. to rush through the air , ἐρροίζητο (3rd singular pluperfect) [variant datesAnthology Palantina (ML)

711286.full: 1. the whistling or whizzing of an arrow, (Iliad by Homer):—;any whistling or piping sound , as of a shepherd, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. rushing motion, a rush, swing , (Plutarch) Formed from the sound. (ML)

s: a large broad sword, used by the Thracians
711291.full: ῥομφαία, -ας, ἡ [in LXX chiefly for חֶרֶב ;] a large broad sword, used by the Thracians (see DB, iv, 634); then generally (in LXX used interchangeably with μάχαιρα, which see), a sword: Rev.1:16 2:12, 16 6:8 19:15, 21; metaphorically, Luk.2:35.† (AS)

711293.full: 1. a club, cudgel , thicker at the buttend; used to cudgel an ass, (Iliad by Homer); to walk with, (Odyssey by Homer), etc.:—; a war-club or mace , shod with metal, (Odyssey by Homer) 2. = ῥόπτρον III, (Xenophon Historicus) (ML)

s: inclination downwards, as the turn of the scale
711294.full: ῥοπή, -ῆς, ἡ (ῥέπω, to incline) [in LXX: Isa.40:15 (שַׁחַק), etc. ;] inclination downwards, as the turn of the scale: L, mg., for ῥιπή, which see, 1Co.15:52 (see Tdf., in l).† (AS)
